Counsel for Applicant :- Sri Shailendra Srivastava,Kaushal Kishore Tewari Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Ajai Kumar Srivastava-I,J.
1. Heard Sri Shailendra Srivastava, learned counsel for the applicant, Sri Alok Saran, learned A.G.A.
for the State-respondent and perused the entire record.
2. Learned counsel for the applicants submits that he wants to delete the applicant no.2 from the array of applicants and also wants to implead the opposite party no.2, who is the first informant of F.I.R. No.0149 of 2018, under Sections 498-A, 323, 354, 504, 506 I.P.C., Police Station Mahila Thana, District Lucknow in the array of opposite parties.
3. The prayer made for is allowed.

4. Learned counsel for the applicants is permitted to delete the applicant no.2 from the array of applicants and also to implead the opposite party no.2 in the array of opposite parties during the course of day.

The instant application under Section 482 Cr.P.C. has been filed by the applicant for quashing the proceedings of the cases pending before the different competent courts between the parties which are mentioned below :

(i) Case No.79183 of 2019, under Sections 498A, 323, 504, 506 I.P.C., Police Station Mahila Thana, District Lucknow pending before Civil Judge (J.D.)/Judicial Magistrate, Fast Track Court, Lucknow.
(ii) Case No.1562 of 2019, arising out of Case Crime No.421 of 2018, under Sections 504, 506 I.P.C., Police Station Gazipur, District Lucknow pending before the Special Chief Judicial Magistrate (Custom), Lucknow.

sentences.text: 6. Learned counsel for the applicant submits that a first information report came to be lodged under Sections 498-A, 323, 354, 504, 506 I.P.C. against the applicant and his relatives.
Upon conclusion of investigation, charge sheet came to be filed against the present applicant only.
His further submission is that the applicant and the complainant have entered into a compromise on 28.03.2023.
They have settled their dispute amicably out of the Court and have decided not to contest the case against each other.
Copy of the compromise dated 28.03.2023 is on record as Annexure No.8 to the instant application.

7. Whether the parties have, in fact, compromised the matter or not, can best be ascertained by the court below, as such, compromise has to be duly verified in presence of the concerned parties before the court below.

8. Accordingly, this application is finally disposed of with a direction to the court concerned that if any such compromise is filed before it, notices be issued to all the signatories to the compromise requiring their personal presence and, thereafter, proceed to verify the compromise.
If the aforesaid compromise is verified, a report to that effect shall be prepared by the court concerned and the compromise will be made part of the record.

9. The court concerned in that scenario will allow the parties to obtain certified copy of the report as well as compromise and it will be open to the applicant to approach this Court again for quashing of the proceedings.

10. The Registry of the Court is directed to return the original compromise deed annexed with the instant application as Annexure No.8 to the learned counsel for the applicant after retaining a photocopy of the same on record.

11. It is also provided that during the process of verification of compromise, process, if any, is found to be issued against the present applicant, the same shall not be given effect to qua the present applicant, namely, Abhishek Shukla.
